_comment: Priority-tier config for state_machine.enqueue_job() (PP-STATEMACHINE-001 Phase 2, todo #1608). Same shape/convention as tgw-models.json: a 'defaults' block of named tiers, entries keyed '<queue_name>:<operation>' pointing at a tier via {"use_default": "<name>"} (or an explicit int priority). enqueue_job() looks this entry up ONLY when the caller doesn't pass priority= explicitly; an explicit priority= argument always wins. No entry for a given '<queue_name>:<operation>' key falls back to 'normal' (100, today's implicit default) -- an unmapped queue is not an error. NOT YET DEPLOYED (deviation logged in the #1608 result manifest): this file needs to be copied to /opt/TGW/config/tgw-queue-priorities.json as a live-deploy step (same category as the worker restarts this packet also defers) -- config/ is not a git-tracked path (tgw-models.json itself isn't in this repo either), so tgw-coder cannot land it directly per its worktree-isolation contract; state_machine.py's loader tolerates the file being absent (falls back to 'normal' for every lookup) so nothing breaks until this is deployed. Also note: as of this packet landing, no enqueue_job() call site anywhere in src/tgw/ passes a non-default `operation=` kwarg -- every call implicitly uses 'run' (enqueue_job's own default). The packet's proposed 'ebay_publish:end_listing'/'ebay_publish:mark_sold' operation names do not exist in this codebase today (grepped: 'ebay_end_listing'/'mark_sold' are http_server.py operator-action strings that write item JSON directly and never enqueue a job with those literal operation values). Entries below are keyed '<queue_name>:run' to match today's real call shape; if/when a queue starts passing a distinct operation= value, add a new '<queue_name>:<that operation>' entry rather than reusing ':run'.
